entry.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures
entry.summary: Alpöge recently announced smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carathéodory conjectures. We present a simpler construction based on a trigonometric function as a seed. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields have an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed smooth surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carathéodory conjecture.

entry.title: Degenerate Umbilic Points of Analytic Surfaces
entry.summary: Umbilics are points of a surface embedded in three space where normal curvatures are independent of direction. The (in)famous Carathéodory Conjecture states that a compact simply connected embedded surface has at least two umbilic points. A counterexample to this conjecture would be a surface whose principal foliation has index two at a single umbilic. All (purported) proofs of the Carathéodory Conjecture are based on analyses of the index of an umbilic, concluding that it is at most one. This investigation gives a much simpler geometric argument that the index of an umbilic on an analytic surface cannot be an integer larger than one, providing new insight into the Carathéodory Conjecture. The results also establish lower bounds for the index of an umbilic based on its degeneracy.

entry.title: A Study of the Carathéodory Conjecture through Non-Rotationally Symmetric Surfaces
entry.summary: Carathéodory's well-known conjecture states that every sufficiently smooth, closed convex surface in three dimensional Euclidean space admits at least two umbilic points. It has been established that the conjecture is true for all rotationally symmetric surfaces; in this paper, we investigate the umbilic points of two families of surfaces without rotational symmetry, and compute their indices. In particular, we find that the family of surfaces of the form $ax^{2k}+by^{2k}+cz^{2k}=1$ with $a,b,c>0$, $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>1}$ admit 14 umbilic points: six of one known form and eight of another. For many tested values of $a,b,c,k$, such umbilic points have indices $-1/2$ and $1$, respectively. We also explore the dependence of the umbilic points on the parameter $ε$ of the surface $ax^2+εx^4+ay^2+εy^4+bz^2=1$. In particular, for both $a<b$ and $a>b,$ there exist exactly two umbilic points with index 1 for $ε$ smaller than certain critical values. For larger $ε,$ surfaces with $a>b$ admit exactly ten umbilic points; for many tested values of $a,b,ε,$ these points have indices 1/2 and -1. For larger $ε,$ surfaces with $a<b$ admit eighteen umbilic points; for many tested values of $a,b,ε,$ these points have indices -1/2 and 1.
